title: TypeScript
summary: The type system: what it guarantees and where its protection ends.
why: Generated code compiles and still lies: types vanish at runtime. Understanding what the compiler guarantees, and what it does not, is how you catch the bugs AI leaves behind.

cards.question: What is the difference between any and unknown?
cards.answer: any turns type checking off. unknown accepts any value but forces you to check or narrow the type before using it, which is why it is the safe alternative.

cards.question: What are utility types? Give examples.
cards.answer: Built-in generic types that transform others: Partial<T> (all optional), Pick<T, K> and Omit<T, K> (select or exclude properties), Record<K, V> and ReturnType<F>.

cards.question: interface or type?
cards.answer: They overlap a lot. Only interface supports declaration merging and natural extends between objects; only type can express unions, mapped and conditional types. What matters is consistency within a project.

cards.question: What does it mean that TypeScript is structurally typed?
cards.answer: Compatibility depends on a value's shape, not the type's name: if an object has the required properties it is assignable even if it never declares implementing the interface.

cards.question: What are generics and constraints for?
cards.answer: They let you write reusable code that preserves the relationship between input and output types instead of losing it with any. extends constrains valid types: <T extends { id: string }>.

cards.question: What is a discriminated union and how do you check exhaustiveness?
cards.answer: A union of types sharing a literal property (for example kind) that lets you narrow the type in a switch. To guarantee exhaustiveness assign the default case to never: if you add a variant and forget to handle it, compilation fails.

cards.question: If I use TypeScript, why must I validate API input?
cards.answer: Types are erased at compile time: they do not exist at runtime, and external JSON can have any shape. Validate at the boundary with a library such as Zod and derive the type from the schema so type and validation never diverge.
